title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-3
content:
Summary / context:
- Working on intermittent correctness issues for long decode requests (>2048 tokens) when using continuous batching + prefix caching. Failures observed as either: (a) outputs diverge from local baseline (determinism/regression), or (b) sudden duplication/garbage tokens mid-stream.
- Likely related to attention kernel selection + KV cache offsets when sequence-length profile crosses thresholds that change the kernel path.
- Repro on staging provided by QA (seeded prompt that eventually reaches ~3.2k tokens after generation).

Observed behavior (high level):
- Single-client local run (no batching) -> baseline correct.
- Multi-client / continuous-batch mode -> ~1/20 requests will start producing wrong tokens after ~token 2100.
- When we force a single kernel (force_kernel=splitkv) the failure rate drops to ~0.5/200. Forcing streamed kernel shows higher failure rate.

Quick logs and snippets:
- Kernel selection debug enabled (LOG_LEVEL=debug kernel_selector):
  [2026-02-17 14:02:11.123] kernel_selector: chosen=cached_splitkv reason=(seqlen=2176, batch_profiles=[{avg=512,max=2048}])
  [2026-02-17 14:02:11.124] kv_cache: alloc base_ptr=0x7f9a1c800000 size=128MB id=pool-46
  [2026-02-17 14:02:11.243] attention_kernel: init splitkv tile_size=64 optimize_for=latency
  [2026-02-17 14:02:12.417] decode: appended 512 tokens to kv, kv_len=2048
  [2026-02-17 14:02:12.423] kernel_selector: re-eval -> chosen=streaming_kv reason=(seqlen=2560 crosses-threshold)
  [2026-02-17 14:02:12.424] kv_cache: reuse base_ptr=0x7f9a1c800000 offset=0x2000 (suspect)
  [2026-02-17 14:02:12.428] runtime_error: attention mismatched QK dims (expected 4096 got 4104)

- Error traces seen in staging job (abridged):
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/srv/serving/runtime/decoder.py", line 328, in step
      out = attention.forward(qkv, kv_cache_ptr)
    File "/srv/serving/runtime/kernels/streaming_kv.py", line 91, in forward
      assert kv_ptr % 64 == 0, f"unaligned kv_ptr {kv_ptr}"
  AssertionError: unaligned kv_ptr 4104

Commands / experiments tried so far:
- Repro script (staging):
  ./tools/run_decode.py --model redwood-open-7b --prompt tests/repro/long-prefix.json --max-new-tokens 3200 --batching continuous --log-kernel-selection
- Force kernel via env var (KERSEL_FORCE=splitkv / KERSEL_FORCE=streaming_kv) -> observed delta in failure rate as noted above.
- Instrumented kv allocator with base/offset dumps (KV_DEBUG=1) and confirmed base_ptr stable but offsets change when kernel switches mid-request.
- Added alignment check in kernel_selector (temp) to prevent switching to streaming_kv if kv_ptr would be misaligned -> prevented crash but masked incorrect outputs (still divergence).
- Local unit test: simulated mixed micro-batch sizes (16, 128, 512) reproduced kernel selection flip.
- Heap-check + valgrind-like sanitizer on host was noisy; kernel C++ path hard to run under ASAN with GPU kernels.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel switch race: switching attention kernel mid-request doesn't update per-kernel stride/padding assumptions -> leads to unaligned pointer or mismatched tile sizes (most likely).
2) KV pointer arithmetic bug: when reusing base_ptr across different kernel lifetimes, the computed offset uses previous kernel tile_size instead of new kernel's tile_size.
3) Padding normalization error: micro-batch padding changed after a merge/split and the KV write offset doesn't account for pad tokens in the forwarded chunk.
4) Scheduler / continuous batching bug: micro-batches from different clients merged into a batch whose aggregated seqlen triggered a kernel change with inconsistent per-sample metadata.

Quick code area suspects:
- serving-runtime/src/kernel_selector.cc  (function choose_kernel_for_batch)
  - logic around seqlen thresholds: if (max_seqlen > STREAMING_THRESHOLD) choose streaming_kv else splitkv
  - missing step: update per-kernel alignment/padder metadata before switching
- serving-runtime/src/kv_cache/allocator.h / .cc  (compute_offset, reuse logic)
  - compute_offset takes (base, sample_idx, pad) -> returns offset_in_bytes
  - ensure it uses current kernel.tile_size not cached one
- kernels/streaming_kv.cu  (assumptions about kv_ptr alignment and layout)

Repro checklist (to get deterministic repro):
- [ ] Add a deterministic harness that simulates continuous batching with controlled interleaving of micro-batches (use --seed and fixed client arrival times).
- [ ] Add kernel_selector verbose dump to include per-sample tile_size/padder before and after switch.
- [ ] Run with KERSEL_FORCE to verify switching path is the only variable.
- [ ] Add a small-mode CPU fallback run (streaming_kv CPU implementation) to replicate pointer math without GPU noise.

Quick mitigation (short-term):
- Prevent kernel switching mid-request: add barrier so kernel selection is sticky for the life of a decode (config flag: enforce_kernel_sticky=true). This reduced incidents in staging.
- Add alignment guard that refuses to reuse a base_ptr when pointer % tile_size != 0 (fall back to allocate new buffer). Slower but safe.

Notes-to-self / next experiments:
- Try forcing different tile_size values to reproduce misalignment calculation: KERNEL_TILE_SIZE_OVERRIDE=32 / 64 / 128. Observe failure boundary.
- Create minimal C++ unit that mirrors allocator::compute_offset and test against both tile_size values.
- Check commit history around kv allocator (last changes in PR 1720) for any refactor touching cached_tile_size.
- Pair with Samir to run GPU repro under cuda-memcheck (he has recipe that reduces false positives).
- Ask SRE to run a targeted flamegraph for scheduler decisions during the failing window.

Breadcrumbs / links / references:
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1623456789000 (thread with initial QA report)
- Jira: INFR-4721 (investigate long-seq KV corruption)
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1720 (kv allocator refactor), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1829 (recent kernel selection metric change)

Short-term notes for release/QA:
- Mark as blocking for 2026-02-26 patch release if mitigation (sticky kernel) not validated by canary.
- Add a regression test in CI that runs the deterministic harness with continuous batching and seeds that previously failed.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is there any GPU-side buffering in the driver that expects a stable tile_size for the lifetime of the kernel launch? (could explain why forcing same kernel helps).
- Are there any other places we cache tile_size per-worker that don't get updated on kernel switch? (global worker struct?).

TODO (action items):
- [Miguel] add verbose kernel_selector dump and push branch (mtorres/kv-kerneldump)
- [Lena] small CPU unit test for allocator::compute_offset (lzhou/kv-offset-test)
- [Samir] run cuda-memcheck with the staging repro and capture nvprof traces (samir/kv-repro)
- [Asha] standardize sticky-kernel flag and run quick canary (asha/sticky-kernel-wip)

Notes end.

(keeping this as a living scratchpad; will move polished findings into Confluence after repro and PRs are opened)
